Hi! I'm Martin — a developer who loves building cool web projects and interactive experiences.

I'm interested in web development, creative coding, and turning fresh ideas into reality.

Looking for teammates to join forces under for the space hackathon.
summary: Universe Explorer is a web app that lets anyone explore real NASA sky data from their room. Users pick any coordinates or a featured target (Andromeda, Orion, the Galactic Center, WISE 0855-0714 and others), and the app pulls live images from NASA SkyView and the unWISE survey, built on NASA’s WISE infrared mission. A side-by-side slider compares visible light (DSS2) with infrared (WISE W1/W2/W3), showing why cold, faint objects like a hypothetical Planet X are hidden in optical light but can show up in infrared, the same wavelengths SPHEREx maps across 102 spectral bands. An AI video model can turn a real sky cutout into a short animated clip, so every visual stays grounded in actual data instead of an invented space scene.
details: What it does: Universe Explorer turns NASA’s infrared archives into an interactive experience. After a short mission-control intro, users target any RA/Dec and field of view, or choose a featured object, and instantly see real sky cutouts. The visible vs infrared slider makes the challenge’s key idea tangible: objects that are dark in visible light, such as brown dwarfs, dusty regions, or a distant cold planet, glow in infrared. How it works: The frontend is React/Vite, hosted on Vercel. Serverless API routes fetch sky cutouts on demand from NASA SkyView (DSS2 optical) and unWISE/WISE infrared imagery for the chosen coordinates. A “Space Video AI” option sends the real cutout to an AI video model, which animates it into a short clip. A built-in guide explains the science (optical extinction, thermal infrared emission, SPHEREx bands) for judges and the public. Benefits and impact: It makes infrared astronomy personal, visual and shareable, with no software or expertise needed. It works on desktop and mobile, and it is a foundation for exploring SPHEREx data as it is released. Future plans: A dedicated domain, plus a full immersive 3D explorer where users can fly through real sky regions built from NASA infrared data, including SPHEREx. Tools: React, Vite, Vercel serverless functions, NASA SkyView, unWISE/Legacy Survey cutout services, Web Audio, and an AI video model. Use of AI: The concept, scientific framing, data pipeline, design and presentation are our team’s own work. We designed how Universe Explorer pulls live NASA SkyView and unWISE/WISE data, built the visible vs infrared comparison, and wrote the science guide explaining Planet X and SPHEREx. We used AI coding assistants as productivity tools while developing the web app, and the optional “Space Video AI” feature uses a third-party AI video model to animate real NASA sky cutouts into short clips, clearly labeled as AI-generated. All scientific imagery in the app is unaltered NASA/WISE data, not AI-generated. Use of Super Intelligence (SI): Coding, Debugging, or Troubleshooting; Building SI/ML Into the Project.
